findings.claim: Analysis of 608 animal subarachnoid-haemorrhage articles found 243 (40.0%) had image-related problems, yet publisher self-correction had largely stalled: only 55 (22.6%) corrected, 19 (7.8%) retracted, and 87.7% of problematic articles had a corresponding author affiliated with an institute in China.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We included 608 articles, of which 243 articles were identified as problematic (40.0%).
findings.evidence: Image-integrity audit of all animal studies in a systematic review of SAH early brain injury.
findings.effect_size: 243/608 (40.0%) problematic; 55 (22.6%) corrected; 19 (7.8%) retracted
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We included 608 articles, of which 243 articles were identified as problematic (40.0%).

findings.claim: Analysis of 1,365 registered PROSPERO protocols for systematic reviews of animal studies found only 694 (51%) resulted in a published review (suggesting publication bias), with a median time to publish of 16.2 months and 69% longer to submission than authors anticipated.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Among these, 694 (51%) resulted in a published systematic review.
findings.evidence: Registry analysis of 1,365 PROSPERO animal-study SR protocols with publication-status search.
findings.effect_size: 694/1365 (51%) protocols published; median publish time 16.2 months
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Among these, 694 (51%) resulted in a published systematic review.
findings.study_system: Systematic reviews of animal studies (PROSPERO registry)

findings.claim: The Experimental Design Assistant (EDA) is a web-based NC3Rs tool that guides in vivo researchers through experimental design and analysis, giving automated feedback and a graphical summary to aid communication with funders and regulators and to address causes of irreproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The EDA is a web-based tool that guides the in vivo researcher through the experimental design and analysis process, providing automated feedback on the proposed design and generating a graphical summary that aids communication with colleagues, funders, regulatory authorities, and the wider scientific community.
findings.evidence: Introduction of the NC3Rs Experimental Design Assistant (design-support infrastructure).

findings.claim: Argues the 3Rs are insufficient for ethical animal research because animal welfare alone does not make research ethical without scientific value; proposes adding Robustness, Registration and Reporting (a 6R framework) to safeguard scientific value.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, animal welfare alone does not suffice to make animal research ethical if the research does not have sufficient scientific value.
findings.evidence: Conceptual proposal extending the 3Rs to a 6R framework (robustness, registration, reporting).

findings.claim: Qualitative interview study exploring 30 animal experiments found blinding (masking) was rarely implemented in some settings, with significant barriers arising from operational and informatic welfare-management systems that prioritise welfare without enabling masking, and a conflict between individual-animal welfare and delivering a robust experiment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Lack of masking has been shown to correlate with an overestimation of treatment efficacy and false positive findings.
findings.evidence: Qualitative interviews across academic and commercial settings exploring 30 experiments and barriers to masking.
findings.effect_size: 30 experiments explored
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We conducted multiple interviews, to explore 30 different experiments, and found examples of excellent practice but also areas where masking was rarely implemented.

findings.claim: Review on designing, conducting and reporting reproducible animal experiments emphasises open research practices, recommending study preregistration, preprints and data management/sharing alongside internal-validity safeguards to improve reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We then discuss the importance of open research practices such as study preregistration and the use of preprints and describe recommendations around data management and sharing.
findings.evidence: Educational review of reproducibility practices for in vivo experiments (design, conduct, reporting, open research).

findings.claim: An international working group of 14 distilled 10 key considerations (the iTRIPP guidelines) for planning and reporting behavioural animal studies in preclinical psychopharmacology, intended to complement general reporting guidelines and improve translational relevance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The following paper distils the outcomes of the working group's discussions into 10 key considerations for the planning and reporting of behavioural studies in animal models relevant to psychiatric disorders.
findings.evidence: Consensus guideline (iTRIPP) from a 14-member working group for preclinical psychopharmacology.
findings.effect_size: 10 key considerations (working group of 14)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The following paper distils the outcomes of the working group's discussions into 10 key considerations for the planning and reporting of behavioural studies in animal models relevant to psychiatric disorders.

findings.claim: Using Experimental Design Assistant case studies, this review shows there is no perfect animal-experiment design and that a harm-benefit analysis is ethically required to justify animal use, with design choices (pseudo-replication, blocking, sex bias, standardisation fallacy) materially affecting the conclusions that can be drawn.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Ethically, when working with animals we need to conduct a harm-benefit analysis to ensure the animal use is justified for the scientific gain.
findings.evidence: Case-study review of animal-experiment design trade-offs using the EDA graphical summaries.

findings.claim: A manual FAIR/openness audit of 555 bioscience papers at one university (2014-2023) found the fraction sharing all relevant data rose significantly from 7% in 2014 to 45% in 2023, with data-availability statements and preprints correlating with more and better data sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The fraction of publications that share all relevant data increased significantly, from 7% in 2014 to 45% in 2023.
findings.evidence: Manual FAIR/openness scoring of 555 University of Edinburgh bioscience papers, benchmarked against the ODDPub automated tool.
findings.effect_size: share all relevant data: 7% (2014) -> 45% (2023)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The fraction of publications that share all relevant data increased significantly, from 7% in 2014 to 45% in 2023.

findings.claim: The preregistration revolution argues that defining hypotheses and analysis plans before observing outcomes separates confirmatory from exploratory analysis and improves credibility of findings.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Widespread adoption of preregistration will increase distinctiveness between hypothesis generation and hypothesis testing and will improve the credibility of research findings.
findings.evidence: Conceptual/methodological article proposing preregistration as governance mechanism across disciplines.

findings.claim: Introduction of open-data/open-materials badges at Psychological Science raised reported open data from under 3% to 39% within about 18 months, an order-of-magnitude increase, with no change in comparison journals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Before badges, less than 3% of Psychological Science articles reported open data.
findings.evidence: Interrupted time-series of one journal adopting badges vs comparison journals.
findings.effect_size: open-data reporting <3% before badges, 23% after, 39% by first half 2015
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: After badges, 23% reported open data, with an accelerating trend; 39% reported open data in the first half of 2015, an increase of more than an order of magnitude from baseline.

findings.claim: The Hong Kong Principles propose five principles for assessing researchers so that hiring/promotion incentives reward research-integrity behaviors (responsible practices, transparent reporting, open science).
findings.claim_source_sentence: We present five principles: responsible research practices; transparent reporting; open science (open research); valuing a diversity of types of research; and recognizing all contributions to research and scholarly activity.
findings.evidence: Consensus framework from the 6th World Conference on Research Integrity.

findings.claim: A 22-member expert panel concluded the current faculty incentive/reward system is misaligned with societal needs and disconnected from the causes of the reproducibility crisis, deriving six principles for assessing scientists.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A burgeoning number of scientific leaders believe the current system of faculty incentives and rewards is misaligned with the needs of society and disconnected from the evidence about the causes of the reproducibility crisis and suboptimal quality of the scientific publication record.
findings.evidence: Expert-panel workshop synthesis of 22 critique documents.
findings.effect_size: 22-member panel; six principles from 22 key documents
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This resulted in six principles for assessing scientists and associated research and policy implications.

findings.claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology aimed to repeat 193 experiments from 53 papers but the data needed to compute effect sizes was publicly accessible for only 4 of 193 experiments, and authors could not supply data for 68% of experiments.
findings.claim_source_sentence: First, many original papers failed to report key descriptive and inferential statistics: the data needed to compute effect sizes and conduct power analyses was publicly accessible for just 4 of 193 experiments.
findings.evidence: Meta-research report of barriers encountered in a large preclinical replication project.
findings.effect_size: data to compute effect sizes publicly accessible for only 4 of 193 experiments
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: First, many original papers failed to report key descriptive and inferential statistics: the data needed to compute effect sizes and conduct power analyses was publicly accessible for just 4 of 193 experiments.

findings.claim: A meta-research analysis finds peer review remains poorly understood, with major gaps around editorial accountability, reviewer bias, and the social/epistemic impact of review, calling for shared standards and data infrastructure.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We identify core themes including editorial responsibility, the subjectivity and bias of reviewers, the function and quality of peer review, and the social and epistemic implications of peer review.
findings.evidence: Conceptual gap analysis of peer-review research.

findings.claim: A systematic review found only 9 of 101 health-research reporting guidelines had been evaluated for the relation between journal endorsement and completeness of reporting, concluding evidence is insufficient to establish that endorsement improves reporting.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Insufficient evidence exists to determine the relation between journals' endorsement of reporting guidelines and the completeness of reporting of published health research reports.
findings.evidence: Systematic review of evaluations of reporting-guideline endorsement effects.
findings.effect_size: only 9 of 101 guidelines evaluated for endorsement-completeness relation; 26 evaluations identified
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The completeness of reporting of only nine of 101 health research reporting guidelines (excluding CONSORT) has been evaluated in relation to journals' endorsement.
findings.study_system: Journal endorsement of reporting guidelines (systematic review)

findings.claim: A systematic scoping review of 50 systematic reviews found 86.0% reported suboptimal adherence to reporting guidelines (CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE, etc.) despite their widespread availability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, 86.0% of studies reported suboptimal levels of adherence to reporting guidelines.
findings.evidence: Scoping review of 50 systematic reviews of guideline adherence.
findings.effect_size: 86.0% of included reviews reported suboptimal adherence
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, 86.0% of studies reported suboptimal levels of adherence to reporting guidelines.

findings.claim: A survey of 116 health-research journals found only 41 (35%) posted online instructions to peer reviewers, and of those only 19/41 (46%) mentioned reporting guidelines, usually vaguely rather than with clear usage instructions.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Only 41/116 journals (35%) provided online instructions.
findings.evidence: Cross-sectional survey of journal instructions to peer reviewers.
findings.effect_size: 41/116 (35%) had online reviewer instructions; 19/41 (46%) mentioned reporting guidelines
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Almost half of the online instructions 19/41 (46%) mentioned reporting guidelines usually as general statements suggesting they may be useful or asking whether authors had followed them rather than clear instructions about how to use them.
findings.study_system: Health-research journals (peer-review instructions on reporting guidelines)

findings.claim: An updated systematic review of reviews (124 studies) found 87.9% reported suboptimal adherence to reporting guidelines, indicating reporting quality remained inadequate 21 years after CONSORT.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that 87.9% of the included studies reported suboptimal adherence to reporting guidelines.
findings.evidence: Systematic review of reviews spanning CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE, ARRIVE, etc.
findings.effect_size: 87.9% of included reviews reported suboptimal adherence
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We found that 87.9% of the included studies reported suboptimal adherence to reporting guidelines.

findings.claim: After ICMJE required data-sharing statements, 68.6% of 487 clinical-trial articles in JAMA/Lancet/NEJM declared data sharing, but rates diverged by funder (NIH-funded 89% vs industry-funded 61%).
findings.claim_source_sentence: A total of 334 of 487 articles (68.6%; 95% CI, 64%-73%) declared data sharing, with nonindustry NIH-funded trials exhibiting the highest rates of declared data sharing (89%; 95% CI, 80%-98%) and industry-funded trials the lowest (61%; 95% CI, 54%-68%).
findings.evidence: Cross-sectional study of DSS implementation in three ICMJE journals.
findings.effect_size: 68.6% declared data sharing (NIH-funded 89%, industry 61%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A total of 334 of 487 articles (68.6%; 95% CI, 64%-73%) declared data sharing, with nonindustry NIH-funded trials exhibiting the highest rates of declared data sharing (89%; 95% CI, 80%-98%) and industry-funded trials the lowest (61%; 95% CI, 54%-68%).
findings.study_system: Clinical trials in JAMA/Lancet/NEJM (ICMJE data-sharing statement)

findings.claim: A manual audit of 250 psychology articles (2014-2017) found transparency practices rare: raw data shared in 2% (4/188), preregistration 3% (5/188), study protocols 0%, and analysis scripts 1%.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Over half of the articles were publicly available (154/237, 65%, 95% confidence interval [CI] = [59%, 71%]); however, sharing of research materials (26/183; 14%, 95% CI = [10%, 19%]), study protocols (0/188; 0%, 95% CI = [0%, 1%]), raw data (4/188; 2%, 95% CI = [1%, 4%]), and analysis scripts (1/188; 1%, 95% CI = [0%, 1%]) was rare.
findings.evidence: Manual coding of a random sample of psychology articles.
findings.effect_size: raw data shared 2% (4/188); preregistration 3% (5/188); protocols 0%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Over half of the articles were publicly available (154/237, 65%, 95% confidence interval [CI] = [59%, 71%]); however, sharing of research materials (26/183; 14%, 95% CI = [10%, 19%]), study protocols (0/188; 0%, 95% CI = [0%, 1%]), raw data (4/188; 2%, 95% CI = [1%, 4%]), and analysis scripts (1/188; 1%, 95% CI = [0%, 1%]) was rare.

findings.claim: A systematic literature review synthesized drivers and inhibitors of open research data sharing/use across 32 studies into eleven categories, arguing incentives must be tailored to discipline-specific barriers.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This study's purpose is to systematically review the literature on individual researchers' drivers and inhibitors for sharing and using open research data.
findings.evidence: Thematic systematic review of 32 open-data studies (2004-2019).
findings.study_system: Open research data adoption (systematic literature review)

findings.claim: The ARRIVE 2.0 explanation-and-elaboration document notes that despite widespread endorsement the impact of the original ARRIVE guidelines on animal-research reporting transparency was limited, prompting revision into 21 items.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite widespread endorsement by the scientific community, the impact of ARRIVE on the transparency of reporting in animal research publications has been limited.
findings.evidence: Guideline companion document for ARRIVE 2.0.
findings.effect_size: 21 items in ARRIVE 2.0
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: It provides further information about each of the 21 items in ARRIVE 2.0, including the rationale and supporting evidence for their inclusion in the guidelines, elaboration of details to report, and examples of good reporting from the published literature.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of survey data estimated 1.97% of scientists admitted fabricating/falsifying data at least once, and up to 33.7% admitted other questionable research practices.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A pooled weighted average of 1.97% (N = 7, 95%CI: 0.86-4.45) of scientists admitted to have fabricated, falsified or modified data or results at least once--a serious form of misconduct by any standard--and up to 33.7% admitted other questionable research practices.
findings.evidence: Meta-analysis of 18 misconduct surveys.
findings.effect_size: 1.97% admitted fabrication/falsification; up to 33.7% admitted other QRPs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A pooled weighted average of 1.97% (N = 7, 95%CI: 0.86-4.45) of scientists admitted to have fabricated, falsified or modified data or results at least once--a serious form of misconduct by any standard--and up to 33.7% admitted other questionable research practices.

findings.claim: A meta-assessment of bias across disciplines found overall biases relatively small but consistent risks that small, early, and highly-cited studies overestimate effects and non-peer-reviewed studies underestimate them.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, we consistently observed a significant risk of small, early, and highly cited studies to overestimate effects and of studies not published in peer-reviewed journals to underestimate them.
findings.evidence: Analysis of a large random sample of meta-analyses across all disciplines.

findings.claim: An empirical study found papers were more likely to report positive results when corresponding authors worked in US states with higher per-capita academic productivity, supporting a link between publication pressure and bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Across all disciplines, papers were more likely to support a tested hypothesis if their corresponding authors were working in states that, according to NSF data, produced more academic papers per capita.
findings.evidence: Ecological analysis of positive-result frequency vs state productivity.
findings.study_system: US research output (publish-or-perish and outcome bias)

findings.claim: Analysis of 531,889 PLOS/BMC articles found data-availability statements became near-universal after mandated policies (93.7% PLOS, 88.2% BMC in 2018) but only 20.8%/12.2% actually linked to data in a repository; repository-linked articles had up to 25.36% higher citations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In 2018 93.7% of 21,793 PLOS articles and 88.2% of 31,956 BMC articles had data availability statements.
findings.evidence: Automated labelling and citation-regression analysis of DAS.
findings.effect_size: DAS present 93.7% PLOS / 88.2% BMC (2018); only 20.8% PLOS / 12.2% BMC linked to repository data
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In 2017 and 2018, 20.8% of PLOS publications and 12.2% of BMC publications provided DAS containing a link to data in a repository.
findings.study_system: PLOS and BMC articles (data-availability statement policy effect)

findings.claim: The ARRIVE revision position paper states that despite considerable community support, the original 2010 ARRIVE guidelines had limited impact on the quality of animal-research reporting, motivating a tiered revision.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite considerable levels of support from the scientific community, the impact on the quality of reporting in animal research publications has been limited.
findings.evidence: Position paper of the ARRIVE revision working group.

findings.claim: A progress review of reproducibility initiatives recalls that Amgen scientists reproduced only 6 of 53 landmark preclinical studies, and evaluates funder/journal/researcher roles in addressing irreproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Since 2012, when scientists from Amgen reported that they were able to reproduce only 6 of 53 "landmark" preclinical studies, the biomedical research community began discussing the scale of the reproducibility problem and developing initiatives to address critical challenges.
findings.evidence: GBSI review of reproducibility initiatives since 2013.
findings.effect_size: 6 of 53 landmark preclinical studies reproduced
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Since 2012, when scientists from Amgen reported that they were able to reproduce only 6 of 53 "landmark" preclinical studies, the biomedical research community began discussing the scale of the reproducibility problem and developing initiatives to address critical challenges.

findings.claim: A cohort study of 7274 due trials on the EU Clinical Trials Register found only 49.5% posted results within the required 12 months, with commercial sponsors far more compliant (68.1%) than non-commercial ones (11.0%).
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of 7274 trials where results were due, 49.5% (95% confidence interval 48.4% to 50.7%) reported results.
findings.evidence: Retrospective cohort study auditing EUCTR results-posting compliance.
findings.effect_size: 49.5% reported results (commercial 68.1% vs non-commercial 11.0%, adjusted OR 23.2)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of 7274 trials where results were due, 49.5% (95% confidence interval 48.4% to 50.7%) reported results.
findings.study_system: EU Clinical Trials Register (results-reporting mandate compliance)

findings.claim: A cross-sectional study of 10,492 trials dual-registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and EUCTR found 16.2% discrepant on completion status, mostly trials completed on ClinicalTrials.gov but still marked ongoing on EUCTR.
findings.claim_source_sentence: 16.2% were discrepant on completion status.
findings.evidence: Cohort of dual-registered trials comparing completion statuses.
findings.effect_size: 16.2% discrepant on completion status; 33.9% of EUCTR-'ongoing' were 'completed' on ClinicalTrials.gov
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, 33.9% of dual-registered trials described as 'ongoing' on EUCTR were listed as 'completed' on ClinicalTrials.gov.

findings.claim: A longitudinal meta-research study of 473 ethically approved Swiss clinical trials (2016-2020) found 91% were registered at all but only 69% prospectively registered, with investigator-sponsored prospective registration rising from 59% to 70% over five years.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of 473 included clinical trials, 432 (91%) were registered at all and 326 (69%) were prospectively registered.
findings.evidence: Cohort of ethics-approved trials with registry linkage.
findings.effect_size: 91% registered, 69% prospectively registered
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of 473 included clinical trials, 432 (91%) were registered at all and 326 (69%) were prospectively registered.

findings.claim: A tracking-tool evaluation of 30 UK universities found that of 1634 due trials on ClinicalTrials.gov only 1.6% (26) had reported results within a year of completion, while 89.8% remained unreported.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In October 2020, the universities included in our study were sponsoring 1634 due trials, only 1.6% (n = 26) of which had reported results within a year of completion.
findings.evidence: Automated tracker of university trial-reporting performance.
findings.effect_size: 1.6% (26/1634) reported within a year; 89.8% unreported
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In October 2020, the universities included in our study were sponsoring 1634 due trials, only 1.6% (n = 26) of which had reported results within a year of completion.

findings.claim: An institutional-dashboard case study of 2,895 trials at 35 German University Medical Centers found prospective registration rose from 33% to 75% on ClinicalTrials.gov, but timely results reporting within 2 years was only 41%.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Across all UMCs, prospective registration increased from 33% (n = 58/178) to 75% (n = 144/193) for trials registered in ClinicalTrials.gov and from 0% (n = 0/44) to 79% (n = 19/24) for trials registered in DRKS over the period considered.
findings.evidence: Semiautomated cohort assessment with interactive dashboard.
findings.effect_size: prospective registration 33% to 75% (ClinicalTrials.gov); timely results reporting 41%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Across all UMCs, prospective registration increased from 33% (n = 58/178) to 75% (n = 144/193) for trials registered in ClinicalTrials.gov and from 0% (n = 0/44) to 79% (n = 19/24) for trials registered in DRKS over the period considered.

findings.claim: A review of FDA New Drug Application efficacy trials found 78% (128/164) were published, with trials having favorable primary outcomes far more likely to be published (OR 4.7), and outcomes/conclusions frequently altered between the NDA and the publication.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Seventy-eight percent (128/164) of efficacy trials contained in FDA reviews of NDAs were published.
findings.evidence: Observational comparison of NDA trial data vs publications.
findings.effect_size: 78% (128/164) published; favorable-outcome trials OR 4.7 for publication

conflicts.paper_a_claim: No manuscript in either group achieved full compliance with the ARRIVE checklist.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: There was an improvement in the reporting of risks of bias in in vivo research in NPG journals following a change in editorial policy, to a level that to our knowledge has not been previously observed.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether journal checklist interventions improve reporting of animal research. IICARus (a randomised trial requesting ARRIVE-checklist completion at submission to PLOS ONE) found no improvement in full ARRIVE compliance, whereas NPQIP found a mandatory Nature checklist at revision raised full 'Landis 4' compliance from 0% to 16.4%. They differ on enforcement (voluntary request vs mandatory), outcome definition (full 108-item ARRIVE vs 4 bias items) and journal.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Unfortunately, publication of ARRIVE guidelines did not seem to enhance reporting quality, compared to papers appeared before ARRIVE publication.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: We find that reporting of randomization, blinding, and sample-size estimation significantly improved when comparing Nature to Cell from 2013 to 2015, likely due to implementation of a checklist.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether ARRIVE/checklists improve reporting. The Chagas review found passive publication of ARRIVE did not improve reporting, while the Nature-vs-Cell study attributed significant improvement to an enforced submission checklist. The divergence maps onto passive dissemination versus active journal enforcement.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Between 1997 and 2020 (where data were readily available in our data set), rigor and transparency measures showed general improvement (RTI 2.29 to 4.13), suggesting that authors are taking the need for improved reporting seriously.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Reporting quality analysis of preclinical studies revealed substantial reporting deficits across all leading journals, with little improvement over the last 20 years, especially for group size calculations, defining primary versus secondary outcomes, and blinded analysis.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether reporting quality of biomedical/preclinical research has improved over roughly two decades. A large automated cross-field metric (Rigor and Transparency Index over >2M papers) detects a general upward trend, whereas a domain-specific manual audit of kidney preclinical studies finds little improvement over 20 years. The divergence maps onto measurement scope and method (whole-literature automated keyword-based scoring vs deep manual scoring of specific design items) and on field.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: 96.5% of research manuscripts appeared to have provided data- and/or code via link or supplementary material
conflicts.paper_b_claim: A study analyzing 7,750 biomedical research papers published between 2015 and 2020 found that only 9% of all papers pledged to make their data publicly available, and a mere 3% of the total followed through with this commitment.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether data-availability policies translate into actual data sharing: enforced mandatory data/code-sharing policies with editorial checks achieve near-universal (96.5%) provision, whereas voluntary data-availability-statement regimes yield only 3-7% of authors actually sharing usable data. The disagreement is on policy effectiveness and is explained by enforcement mechanism (mandatory-at-review vs voluntary statement).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The fraction of publications that share all relevant data increased significantly, from 7% in 2014 to 45% in 2023.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Meta-analyses showed a prevalence of declared and actual public data availability of 8% (95% confidence interval 5% to 11%) and 2% (1% to 3%), respectively, between 2016 and 2021.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether research data sharing is substantially improving. A single-institution manual audit (University of Edinburgh biosciences) finds a strong rise to 45% of papers sharing all relevant data by 2023, whereas a field-wide IPD meta-analysis of medical/health research finds actual public data availability stuck at ~2%. The divergence maps onto scope (one progressive institution vs whole literature) and metric definition ('all relevant data' incl. supplementary/genomic deposits vs verified reusable public availability).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The organizational premise is that rigorous high-quality research is more likely to produce tangible benefit than poor quality, low rigor research.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Because of the limitations of the review process, funding institutions and scientific journals should not use Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee approval of submissions as evidence of adherence to ethical guidelines beyond those legally required.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether ethics-committee/IACUC review can be trusted to safeguard the scientific quality (and hence benefit) of animal research. One proposes a Benefit Assessment Matrix presuming committees can and should assess research rigor/benefit; the other argues US IACUCs structurally lack the expertise and mandate to judge scientific merit, so their approval should not be taken as evidence of ethical adherence. The disagreement is on the feasibility of quality/benefit judgement within existing oversight bodies.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Before badges, less than 3% of Psychological Science articles reported open data.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: We found that 87.9% of the included studies reported suboptimal adherence to reporting guidelines.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Efficacy of transparency interventions: an enforced, incentivised journal signal (open-practice badges) produced an order-of-magnitude jump in open-data sharing at one journal, whereas two decades of voluntary reporting-guideline availability left ~88% of the literature with suboptimal adherence - implying guideline existence alone is far weaker than enforced incentives.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Insufficient evidence exists to determine the relation between journals' endorsement of reporting guidelines and the completeness of reporting of published health research reports.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Information about ethical statement and 3R's Principles Before ARRIVE guidelines became widely available, approximately 51% of papers on animal models evaluating drugs for Chagas disease included a statement about compliance with local or international guidelines for experimentation with animals.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether journal endorsement/publication of reporting guidelines improves reporting: a systematic review finds insufficient evidence that endorsement is linked to completeness, while a before/after ARRIVE study finds guideline publication produced no significant improvement (51%->66%, p=0.26) - both undercut the assumption that endorsement drives better reporting but disagree on whether any endorsement-completeness signal exists at all.

evidence_gaps.topic: Infrastructure and roadmaps for preclinical data reuse
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Few primary studies quantify reuse of shared preclinical/animal datasets or evaluate repository infrastructure; most evidence measures availability, not downstream reuse.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Reuse is the mechanism by which FAIR data reduces animal waste; without reuse metrics, data-sharing mandates may not translate into fewer animals used.

evidence_gaps.topic: Causal effect of reporting-guideline endorsement on reporting quality
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Only two randomised/controlled intervention designs (IICARus, NPQIP-related) exist; most evidence is before/after cross-sections confounded by secular trends.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Policy is being set (mandatory checklists) on largely observational evidence with conflicting results.

evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Primary quantitative evidence that ethical-review-body scrutiny improves 3Rs implementation or reduces animal numbers is sparse; most studies survey attitudes.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Governance bodies are the front-line control on animal use, but their measured impact on waste/quality is largely undocumented (false_consensus_risk).

strongest_evidence.claim: Actual public data availability in medical/health research is only ~2% (declared 8%), with public code sharing <0.5%, and policies encouraging sharing are no more effective than none.
strongest_evidence.why_strong: Systematic review with IPD meta-analysis of 105 meta-research studies covering 2.1M articles across 31 specialties (10.1136/bmj-2023-075767), converging with independent PLOS ONE (10.1371/journal.pone.0194768) and oncology (10.1186/s12916-022-02644-2) analyses.

weakest_evidence_cited.claim: NTS systematic-analysis method can support AWERB scrutiny of licence applications.
weakest_evidence_cited.why_weak: Single proof-of-concept applied to one disease domain (respiratory) with no outcome measure of improved oversight or reduced animal use (10.1177/02611929221121076).
